newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Afghan Taleban asks members not to be harsh.
newsitem.headline: Afghan Taleban asks members not to be harsh.

text.p: Afghanistan's radical Islamic Taleban movement told its members on Tuesday to relax their harsh treatment of people in the capital Kabul, official Kabul Radio said.
The broadcast, monitored in Islamabad, quoted Taleban leader Mullah Mohammad Omar as telling his followers to "behave with the disturbed citizens of (war-shattered) Kabul so you get Allah's mercy".
He told Taleban members to behave in accordance with Islamic Sharia law and not to harm or tease residents of the capital.
The radio also quoted another Taleban statement advising the movement's fighters to avoid harsh treatment of citizens, particularly women.

The Taleban enforced a strict Islamic code after capturing Kabul in late September from the government of President Burhanuddin Rabbani, ordering women not to come out of their homes without a veil and forcing men to grow long beards and offer prayers in mosques.
The moves aroused worldwide protests from human rights groups.

Tuesday's Taleban order for a relaxation coincided with a statement by the United Nations Children's Fund (UNICEF) that it would only release funds for education in Afghanistan when the Taleban allowed girls back into schools.
UNICEF is seeking $10.1 million to boost its aid programme for Afghan women and children, whose situation continues to be "among the worst in the world", according to the agency.
It is among several U.N. agencies taking part in a $133 million appeal to donor countries launched on Tuesday.

UNICEF's educational aid has been suspended since November 1995 in areas where girls are excluded from attending school, two months after Taleban forces seized the main western town of Herat and closed girls' schools there.

The policy has been extended to include Kabul, which the Taleban militia captured on September 27, proclaiming themselves the new rulers of the war-torn country. UNICEF's educational support is limited to the northern region, the area not under Taleban control.
